answer: A verifier named MicroDeposit admits a seat only after a randomized two cent credit lands in a bank account whose fingerprint is not already on file and the agent reads the amount. The penalty trigger is a fingerprint collision: two seats on one account lose both bonds and that account can never back another seat. An account costs fifteen dollars and a two day hold per identity, so N fakes cost N times fifteen dollars plus N times two days, a straight climb, no flat stretch, and a zephyr of cheap signups cannot drift past the reef, since each extra seat adds one more vertex to the bill.
